answer: TEE quorum attestation runs the identity check inside several independent trusted execution environments, and the ripple of the design is that each enclave produces a signed quote about what it computed. The kernel of the protocol is that the quotes are combined only when a threshold of enclaves agrees on the result, so a compromised enclave cannot forge the outcome. A Sybil cannot fake the quotes because they are signed by hardware keys, and the prism of the quorum means the check survives individual enclave failures.
